name: San Juan Quiahije Chatino Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Sign language (Hou 2016, Mesh 2017 describe it); word stress category inapplicable and no stress statement exists

sources.citation: Glottolog languoid record chat1269 (Sign Language > L1 Sign Language); no descriptive references listed

Mesh, Kate & Lynn Hou. 2018. Negation in San Juan Quiahije Chatino Sign Language: The integration and adaptation of conventional gestures. Gesture 17(3): 330-374. doi:10.1075/gest.18017.mes (Lund University open postprint)
sources.note: No word-stress statement. Footnote 7 (p. 348) only uses phrase-level prosodic boundary markers (hand lowering, pausing, torso shift) to segment utterances; fn. 2 notes spoken SJQ Chatino is a tone language (irrelevant to the sign language).

sources.citation: Mesh, Kathryn. 2017. Points of comparison: What indicating gestures tell us about the origins of signs in San Juan Quiahije Chatino Sign Language. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Austin. 244 pp. (hdl:2152/63635; fetched sources via Wayback Machine copy)
sources.note: Nothing about SJQCSL prosody or stress; three studies of indicating (pointing) gestures and signs. The only 'stressed syllables' mention concerns gesture-speech timing in spoken language literature.

sources.citation: Hou, Lynn Y-S. 2016. "Making hands": Family sign languages in the San Juan Quiahije community. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Austin. 358 pp. (hdl:2152/46879; fetched sources via Wayback Machine copy of the UT repository bitstream)
sources.note: Nothing. Chapters are ethnography, signing community/families, lexical (sublexical) variation, pointing/directionality, language ideologies; full-text search for stress/prosod/accent/suprasegment/prominen finds no linguistic use (only 'stresses the value of ethnographic research').

sources.citation: Hou, Lynn. 2018. Iconic Patterns in San Juan Quiahije Chatino Sign Language. Sign Language Studies 18(4): 570-611.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; Harvard e-access not checked
sources.note: Only remaining unopened description of SJQCSL sign form; very unlikely to contain a stress/prominence statement (topic is iconicity), but it is the one formal-structure paper not checked.
